newsitem.title: FRANCE: French businesses suffer from truck strike.
newsitem.headline: French businesses suffer from truck strike.

text.p: French businesses were forced to introduce short-time working after being starved of fuel and raw materials as the French truck drivers strike went into its 10th day on Wednesday.

Half of the 400 petrol depots in France were blockaded by the truck drivers, notably in the southeast, the Rhone Valley, but also in the southwest, Brittany, Normandy and the north, a source close to the government said.
The number of France's 18,000 petrol stations facing temporary closure or shortage rose to nearly 2,000 on Wednesday.
Of the 13 French oil refineries, only the plant in Feyzin, near Lyon in central France, was unaffected by the conflict.

Another strike, led by workers at the refineries of France's largest oil firm Elf Aquitaine, protesting against job cuts, forced it to close its Grandpuits plant near Paris for 24 hours and affected its Donges refinery in the West of France.
The food industry was one of the sectors worst hit by the shortages of fuel.

"It's getting crazy everywhere," Philippe Cousseau, president of agro-food group ANIA. "Our transporters have no more fuel. If the situation doesn't ease tomorrow, nobody will be able to deliver food products. We will have practically a total blockage at factories."

In the Bouches-du-Rhone region of southern France, more than a thousand people will likely be working part time or stopping altogether by the end of the week, according to the regional employers federation.
"Lots of companies have serious problems," such as the clock maker Beuchat which says it's in a "catastrophic situation", a spokesman said.
In the central Rhone region, employers were concerned about the "short-term difficulties for exporters".
The Lyon Chamber of Commerce said deliveries of components were delayed, notably at car parts maker Valeo and Renault's truck making division, and that there were risks of food stocks running out.
School buses stopped running in the southeastern Drome department and there will only be a partial service on Thursday because of fuel shortages and road blocks.

The president of shopkeepers union Cid-Unati, Jacques Gerbault, advised shopkeepers to use domestic fuel in their professional vehicles, a practice strictly outlawed because of the difference in taxation.
The firm "Le petit Basque" which makes desserts in the Gironde region was unable to deliver its products in several regions. It said turnover had fallen 40 percent in a week.
Strawberry wholesaler Picon SA at Vergt in the Dordogne said it estimated it had lost 2.5 million francs ($500,000) in turnover and predicted short-term layoffs for 50 workers.
However, in the Lot-et-Garonne region in southwest France the chamber of commerce and industry said there were no major problems with trains relaying produce.
Peugeot's factories at Sochaux and Mulhouse were functioning normally for now.
In the north, Renault's factory at Douai, which employs 6,000 people remained closed for the third day in a row because of a truck blockade which prevented supplies getting through.
Another firm in the automobile sector, MCA at Maubeuge had to put its 2,700 employers on short-time shifts for the third consecutive day.
